gloss: to blow into; to instill; to record (audio)

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {吹|ふ}き{込|こ}みませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {吹|ふ}き{込|こ}んでいなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {吹|ふ}き{込|こ}んでいませんでした

definitions.gloss: to blow into, to blow in
definitions.explanation: Wind, air, rain, or snow entering a space through an opening. Used both transitively (blow air into something) and intransitively (wind blows in).

definitions.gloss: to instill, to put (ideas) into someone's head
definitions.explanation: To influence someone by repeatedly telling them something, often with the implication of manipulation or indoctrination.
To record sound onto a medium. Used for recording music, voice tracks, or audio.

examples.japanese: {窓|まど}から{風|かぜ}が{吹|ふ}き{込|こ}む。
examples.english: Wind blows in through the window.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}が{部屋|へや}に{吹|ふ}き{込|こ}んできた。
{風船|ふうせん}に{空気|くうき}を{吹|ふ}き{込|こ}む。
{変|へん}な{考|かんが}えを{吹|ふ}き{込|こ}まれた。
examples.english: Strange ideas were put into my head.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもに{偏見|へんけん}を{吹|ふ}き{込|こ}むべきではない。
examples.english: You shouldn't instill prejudices in children.

examples.japanese: {誰|だれ}かが{余計|よけい}なことを{吹|ふ}き{込|こ}んだに{違|ちが}いない。
examples.english: Someone must have put unnecessary ideas in their head.

examples.japanese: スタジオで{曲|きょく}を{吹|ふ}き{込|こ}む。
examples.english: Record a song in the studio.

examples.japanese: ナレーションを{吹|ふ}き{込|こ}む。
{新|あたら}しいアルバムのために{全|ぜん}10{曲|きょく}を{吹|ふ}き{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: I recorded all 10 tracks for the new album.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{風|かぜ}が{吹|ふ}き{込|こ}む (wind blows in)
・{空気|くうき}を{吹|ふ}き{込|こ}む (blow in air)
・{命|いのち}を{吹|ふ}き{込|こ}む (breathe life into)
・{変|へん}な{考|かんが}えを{吹|ふ}き{込|こ}む (put strange ideas into one's head)
・{曲|きょく}を{吹|ふ}き{込|こ}む (record a song)

USAGE NOTES:
Sense 1 is the most literal. Sense 2 almost always has a negative nuance — the ideas being instilled are unwanted, misleading, or manipulative. The expression {命|いのち}を{吹|ふ}き{込|こ}む (breathe life into) bridges senses 1 and 2, meaning to revitalize something. Sense 3 (recording) comes from the early days of audio recording when sound was literally blown into a horn.
